**Analysis of Revenue Growth (FY2022 → FY2024):**

| Airline | FY2022 Revenue | FY2024 Revenue | 2-Yr Growth % | FY2023→FY2024 YoY % |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Delta | $50,582M | $61,643M | 21.9% | 6.2% |
| United | $44,955M | $57,063M | 26.9% | 6.2% |
| Southwest | $23,814M | $27,483M | 15.4% | 5.3% |
| American | $48,971M | $54,211M | 10.7% | 2.7% |
| Alaska | $9,646M | $11,735M | 21.7% | 12.6% |

[DOC-1] "Total operating revenue: FY2022 $50,582M, FY2023 $58,048M, FY2024 $61,643M" (Delta); "FY2022 $44,955M, FY2023 $53,717M, FY2024 $57,063M" (United); "FY2022 $23,814M, FY2023 $26,091M, FY2024 $27,483M" (Southwest); "FY2022 $48,971M, FY2023 $52,788M, FY2024 $54,211M" (American); "FY2022 $9,646M, FY2023 $10,426M, FY2024 $11,735M" (Alaska).

**Important comparability caveat:** Alaska's FY2024 figures are **not organically comparable** to the other carriers or to its own prior years, because Alaska completed its acquisition of Hawaiian Holdings on September 18, 2024, and Hawaiian's results are consolidated into Alaska's financials only from that date forward. [DOC-2] "On September 18, 2024, Alaska Air Group completed its acquisition of Hawaiian Holdings... For the period from the acquisition date to December 31, 2024, revenue... from Hawaiian recognized in the Company's consolidated results of operations was $869 million."

Backing this out, Alaska's **organic** revenue growth (excluding the ~$869M Hawaiian contribution) for 2023→2024 would be roughly (11,735 − 869 − 10,426) / 10,426 ≈ **4.2%**, versus the reported (inorganic) 12.6% — meaning Alaska's headline growth is significantly inflated by M&A rather than organic momentum.

Once Alaska's figures are adjusted for the acquisition, **United Airlines** shows the strongest revenue growth on both a two-year cumulative basis (26.9%, the highest of all five carriers) and matches Delta for the strongest year-over-year growth (6.2%) among organically comparable results. Delta is essentially tied with United on YoY growth but trails on the two-year figure. Southwest, American, and (organically) Alaska show comparatively weaker momentum.

ANSWER: United Airlines had the strongest revenue growth momentum through FY2024 (26.9% growth from FY2022–FY2024, the highest among the five), though Delta showed comparable year-over-year (FY2023–FY2024) growth. Alaska's reported 21.7% two-year growth and 12.6% YoY growth are not directly comparable to peers because they are inflated by the Hawaiian Holdings acquisition (completed Sept. 18, 2024, contributing $869M in revenue); Alaska's organic growth is closer to ~4% YoY, well below United's.
